payload.title: Oracle against Tyre and Nebuchadnezzar

payload.name: Ezekiel son of Buzi
payload.note: Exiled priest and prophet at the river Chebar.

stages.label: Ezekiel son of Buzi

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
payload.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
payload.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

payload.name: Nebuchadnezzar
payload.note: King of Babylon who conquers Jerusalem and destroys the temple; recurs across Kings, Chronicles, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Daniel.

stages.label: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon

quotes.quote: the king of Babylon had taken, from the brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates
King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, worshiped Daniel

stages.text: Nebuchadnezzar: a mature man in his forties to fifties; broad, strong build; olive-bronze skin; dark hair and a full, carefully curled beard in Babylonian royal style; a broad, dignified face with heavy-lidded eyes. Signature outfit: a long crimson and gold court robe over a white linen tunic, with a tall royal crown of gold and lapis. Carries a gold-headed staff of office.

aliases: the region of Tyre and Sidon
the borders of Tyre and Sidon
payload.name: Tyre
payload.note: Phoenician trading city on the coast, judged by the prophets (Isaiah 23, Ezekiel 26-28, Amos 1), with a fallen-merchant-city portrayal in Ezekiel; the same Tyre and Sidon region is visited in Mark and a port stop in Acts. All entries describe one place.

stages.label: Tyre

quotes.quote: Howl, you ships of Tarshish! For it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in.
They will destroy the walls of Tyre, and break down her towers.
I will send a fire on the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its palaces.
You who dwell at the entry of the sea, who are the merchant of the peoples to many islands

stages.text: Tyre: a coastal and island city of Phoenicia on a rocky shore where the sea meets the land, its harbour crowded with merchant ships and its walls built of pale limestone and dark basalt. Stone towers rise along the seaward walls, palaces stand high within, and the land behind is thin scrub, olive and cedar on the hills.

payload.title: Order of the camps by standards

payload.name: Moses
payload.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

payload.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
payload.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

quotes.quote: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron
Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
payload.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
payload.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
payload.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
payload.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

aliases: the door of the Tent of Meeting
the court of the Tent of Meeting
payload.name: the tabernacle (portable sanctuary)
payload.note: The one portable sanctuary of the wilderness, described in Exodus 25-40 and referred to as the Tent of Meeting in Leviticus and Numbers; all three entries are the same place.

stages.label: The tabernacle (portable sanctuary)

quotes.quote: made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet. They made them with cherubim
He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle.
He made the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side southward.
the sockets around the court, the sockets of the gate of the court, all the pins of the tabernacle

stages.text: The tabernacle: a portable sanctuary of a rectangular tent of fine twined linen curtains in blue, purple and scarlet woven with cherubim, over a covering of goats' hair and rams' skins, stretched over upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets and held by gold-covered bars, enclosed by a court of white linen hangings on bronze pillars.

payload.title: Blessings and curses proclaimed on Ebal and Gerizim

aliases: the priests who bear the ark
payload.name: The priests and Levites (Deuteronomy)
payload.note: The Levitical priests who bear the ark and minister and judge in Deuteronomy's ritual and legal scenes.

stages.label: The priests and Levites

quotes.quote: the priests the sons of Levi, who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant
You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant

stages.text: The priests and Levites: adult men of middle age, sturdy and dignified; olive-brown skin of the Levant; close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a white woven linen tunic and sash with a blue-violet priestly robe and cloak, plain and clean. Carry the ark's poles on the shoulder.

payload.name: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy
payload.note: Tribal judges and officers who hear cases and receive the law in Deuteronomy.

stages.label: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy

quotes.quote: then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges
then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place.

stages.text: Elders, judges and officers: men of middle to advanced age, mostly weathered and grey-bearded; sturdy build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beards and close-cropped hair; calm, serious faces. Signature outfit: a long woven undertunic of undyed linen under a deep indigo cloak with a plain woven border. Carry a short wooden staff of office.

payload.name: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim
payload.note: The twin mountains in Deuteronomy where blessings and curses are proclaimed; distinct from the Judges Mount Gerizim, which is the same mountain only by name and is kept apart as a separate setting of Jotham's parable.

stages.label: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim

quotes.quote: you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim, and the curse on Mount Ebal.
These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people
These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse

stages.text: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim: two bare limestone ridges of the central hill country rising opposite each other across a narrow valley. Terraced slopes of olive and fig, scrub of thyme and oak; on Ebal, a plain stone altar and great stones set upright and coated with white plaster, catching the light.

payload.name: The plains of Moab
payload.note: Eastern camp across the Jordan where Moses speaks the law and dies, Deuteronomy only.

stages.label: The plains of Moab

quotes.quote: Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to declare this law
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.
in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites

stages.text: The plains of Moab: a broad, low valley of dry grassland and scrub east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho and Beth Peor, with acacia, tamarisk and wild shrubs along the river line. Rising to the west, the bare slopes of Mount Nebo and Pisgah, with a flat-topped summit, look over the Jordan valley. Plain tents of goat hair and rough stone walls mark the Israelite encampment; no buildings of note stand in the valley.

payload.title: Moses pleads for the people; God's plague

aliases: the tent of meeting outside the camp
payload.name: the camp of Israel
payload.note: The Israelite encampment in the wilderness, with the tent of meeting set outside it in Exodus 33; the same encampment that Leviticus calls the camp.

stages.label: the camp of Israel

quotes.quote: the pillar of cloud moved from before them, and stood behind them.
quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.
Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp
outside of the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out

stages.text: the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.

payload.title: Register of priests, Levites and temple servants

payload.name: the priests (group)
payload.note: The priestly class of the sons of Aaron who perform the rites of offering in Leviticus and who repair gates, take part in processions and sign the covenant in Nehemiah; both entries are the same priestly body, so they are one cluster.

stages.label: the priests (group)

quotes.quote: Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood
and some of the priests’ sons with trumpets

stages.text: The priests: adult men, mostly between thirty and fifty, sturdy and unhurried in bearing. Olive to deep bronze skin, short dark or greying beard, close-cropped hair under a linen head covering. Calm, dignified faces. Signature outfit: a white linen tunic and sash, with a plain linen mitre, in cream and off-white. Props: a bronze censer or a trumpet for processional scenes.

aliases: Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah and the Levites
payload.name: The Levites who teach the law (Nehemiah)
payload.note: Levites in Nehemiah who explain the law, lead prayer and confession, and appear in the register of priests and Levites; they are a teaching and prayer group rather than the tabernacle service crew.

stages.label: The Levites who teach the law

quotes.quote: Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law
Then Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani of the Levites stood up on the stairs, and cried with a loud voice to Yahweh their God.

stages.text: The Levites who teach the law: men of middle age, lean and sure-footed, with brown skin weathered by the Judean sun. Dark hair worn to the shoulder, beards trimmed short and neat. Plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist, over it a long wool cloak in undyed brown or ochre. Carry a wooden staff or a scroll case of leather.

payload.name: Judah (kingdom and land)
payload.note: The kingdom or land of Judah as a single place across Nehemiah, Isaiah, Joel, Habakkuk and Zephaniah; all entries describe the same territory, distinguished only by the section context in which they appear.

stages.label: Judah

quotes.quote: Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field
its gates have been consumed with fire
some of the children of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns

stages.text: Judah: a hill country of terraced slopes, stony ridges and deep valleys, with walled towns and villages set among olive groves, vineyards and grain fields; Jerusalem on its heights with stone walls, gates and a temple, and fortified citadels; cypress, terebinth and cedar on the uplands.

payload.title: Yahweh is a refuge and will consume the enemy

payload.name: Nineveh (Assyrian capital)
payload.note: The Assyrian capital city of Nineveh; all four entries refer to the same city, appearing in Isaiah, Jonah, Nahum and Zephaniah, and are joined as one place.

stages.label: Nineveh, the great Assyrian capital

quotes.quote: The populous city will be deserted. The hill and the watchtower will be for dens forever
The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.
Nineveh has been from of old like a pool of water
make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as the wilderness.

stages.text: Nineveh: a vast walled Assyrian capital on a broad plain beside great rivers, with high mud-brick walls, towering gates of cut stone with winged bull guardians, a royal palace on a raised mound, and a watchtower on a hill. Its moats and river gates hold water like a pool. Date palms, reeds and irrigated fields line the riverbanks; the later ruins are dry, windswept wilderness with dens and wild grass.

payload.title: God's promise and the fate of the wicked

payload.name: John the seer (Revelation)
payload.note: Author and visionary on Patmos who receives and records the revelation; the narrator of Revelation, distinct from other Johns.

stages.label: John the seer

quotes.quote: to his servant, John
I John, your brother and partner with you in the oppression

stages.text: John the seer: man of about sixty, of middle height and spare build, weathered olive skin from exile by the sea, short greying hair and a close grey beard, lined brow and steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a rough dark brown wool mantle. He carries a worn wooden staff and a small scroll case.

payload.name: New Jerusalem
payload.note: Holy city descending from heaven with twelve gates (Revelation).

stages.label: New Jerusalem

quotes.quote: I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God
showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God
the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from my God
out of the holy city, which are written in this book

stages.text: New Jerusalem: a great and high city descending out of heaven, luminous and pure as crystal, its walls of jasper set on twelve foundations adorned with precious stones, and twelve gates of pearl. Its streets are pure gold, clear as glass, with no temple and no sun or moon, lit by the glory of God. Beside it flows a river of life, clear as crystal, and on its banks stands the tree of life bearing fruit each month.

payload.title: Envy of the prosperous wicked resolved

payload.name: Asaph
payload.note: Levitical singer to whom psalms 50 and 73 to 83 are attributed; the psalmist, distinct from the family of Korah.

stages.label: Asaph, Levitical psalmist

quotes.quote: A Psalm by Asaph.

stages.text: Asaph: a man of middle years, broad-shouldered and steady; olive skin, dark close-cropped beard with grey beginning at the chin, deep-set thoughtful eyes and a worn, weathered face. Plain undyed linen tunic with a dark blue-grey wool cloak, Levitical singer's linen. Carries a ten-stringed lyre of cedar wood.

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion
the house of Yahweh of Armies
payload.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
payload.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

payload.title: The priestly law on holiness and the promise to Zerubbabel

payload.name: Haggai
payload.note: The prophet Haggai of the Book of Haggai and Ezra 5-6, who speaks Yahweh's word to Zerubbabel and Joshua in Judah and Jerusalem to press the temple rebuilding; both entries are the same prophet.

stages.label: Haggai the prophet

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came by Haggai the prophet
Then Haggai, Yahweh’s messenger, spoke Yahweh’s message to the people

stages.text: Haggai: a man of middle age, perhaps fifty, lean and weathered from travel. Brown-olive skin, short-cropped dark hair greying at the temples, a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey. Deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist under a rough brown wool cloak, worn in every scene. Carries a simple wooden staff.

payload.name: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel
payload.note: Governor of Judah who leads the return from exile and the temple rebuilding; the single individual across Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai and Zechariah, distinguished from the high priest Joshua.

stages.label: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel

quotes.quote: I will take you, Zerubbabel my servant, the son of Shealtiel
to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah
will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you

stages.text: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and steady in bearing; olive skin weathered by travel; dark hair and a short, neatly kept beard with some early grey; a grave, resolute face with deep-set dark eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak fastened at the shoulder, with a governor's embroidered band of red and gold at the hem. Carries alone a bronze signet ring on his right hand.

payload.name: the priests consulted in Haggai
payload.note: Priests asked for a ruling on holiness and uncleanness in Haggai.

stages.label: the priests consulted in Haggai

quotes.quote: Ask now the priests concerning the law
The priests answered, "No."

stages.text: the priests consulted in Haggai: a typical member is a man in middle age, lean and dignified, with a weathered brown skin, closely trimmed dark beard and short dark hair beneath a plain white linen turban. His signature outfit is a long white linen priestly tunic with a dark blue woven sash, worn over a plain undergarment.

payload.title: Agrippa's response; Paul's words to the court

payload.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
payload.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

payload.name: King Agrippa
payload.note: Herodian king who hears Paul's defense.

stages.label: King Agrippa

quotes.quote: King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp

stages.text: King Agrippa: a man in his early forties; lean, upright build; olive skin; dark hair cut short and a neatly trimmed dark beard with grey at the chin; composed, watchful face with heavy brows. Signature outfit: a fine white linen tunic under a purple-bordered royal cloak of deep violet, with a gold fibula at the shoulder. Carries a plain ceremonial staff of dark wood with a gold cap.

payload.name: Bernice
payload.note: Sister of King Agrippa who attends the hearing with him.

stages.label: Bernice

quotes.quote: King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp

stages.text: Bernice: a woman of about forty, dignified and composed; olive-brown skin; dark hair drawn up and bound with gold pins beneath a fine linen veil edged in purple; a tall, straight-backed build; a poised, aristocratic face with dark, steady eyes. Signature outfit: a long layered tunic of deep purple wool under a pale ivory mantle with a gold-thread border. Signature prop: a slim gold diadem at her brow.

payload.name: Porcius Festus
payload.note: Roman governor who succeeds Felix and refers Paul's case to King Agrippa; a different governor from Pilate and from Gedaliah.

stages.label: Porcius Festus

quotes.quote: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

stages.text: Porcius Festus: a man of about fifty, middle-aged and of sturdy, practical build; olive-brown skin; short dark hair with grey at the temples, closely cropped; a clean-shaven face with a firm jaw and a thoughtful, weathered brow. Signature outfit: a deep purple-edged white toga over a plain ochre tunic, with a bronze fibula at the shoulder. Signature prop: a small wax writing tablet bound in leather.

payload.name: Caesarea Maritima
payload.note: Coastal Roman port city on the Mediterranean, where Cornelius lives, Herod dies, and Paul is held; distinct from Caesarea Philippi in the north.

stages.label: Caesarea Maritima

quotes.quote: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,
he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat

stages.text: Caesarea Maritima: a Roman port city on the Mediterranean coast of Judea, built of pale limestone and mortar. A broad curved harbour with stone moles and wooden-hulled fishing boats, a white-stone city of colonnaded streets, a Roman theatre facing the sea, administrative halls, and bathhouses with arched roofs. Low sea grasses and palms along the shore, dry Mediterranean scrub on the inland rise.

payload.title: War against Benjamin

payload.name: Tribe of Benjamin
payload.note: The Benjamite tribe as a collective in Judges, nearly destroyed in the Gibeah war and rebuilt by seizing wives at Shiloh; not an individual, so kept apart from Benjamin the son of Jacob.

stages.label: Tribe of Benjamin

quotes.quote: The children of Benjamin were counted on that day out of the cities twenty-six thousand men who drew the sword

stages.text: Tribe of Benjamin: men of fighting age and mature adults, lean and sinewy from farming and war; sun-browned olive skin; short dark beards and cropped hair, some with a headband; serious, weathered faces; a plain woven wool tunic in undyed brown and cream under a rust-red cloak; carries a sling or short sword.

aliases: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
payload.name: Phinehas son of Eleazar
payload.note: Priest, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron; appears in Numbers (Baal Peor, Midian), Joshua (Jordan altar dispute) and Judges (Benjamin war at Bethel). Same priestly lineage and role across all three, so one individual.

stages.label: Phinehas, priest of the Aaronic line

quotes.quote: he rose up from the middle of the congregation, and took a spear in his hand.
to the war, with the vessels of the sanctuary and the trumpets for the alarm in his hand.

stages.text: Phinehas: a man in middle age, strong and steady, of Israelite desert-born build; olive-brown skin; dark hair and a short trimmed beard streaked with grey; calm, weathered face. Signature outfit: a white linen priestly tunic with a blue-violet robe and a linen mitre. Carries a spear and the sanctuary trumpets.

aliases: the husband of the murdered woman
the man from the hill country of Ephraim
payload.name: The Levite husband of the concubine
payload.note: Levite from the hill country of Ephraim whose concubine is abused and killed at Gibeah; he cuts her body into twelve pieces. Not the young Levite of Bethlehem who serves Micah.

stages.label: The Levite husband of the concubine

quotes.quote: The Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered

stages.text: The Levite husband of the concubine: a man in his thirties, lean and weathered by travel, with olive skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard shot with grey at the chin. Calm, grave features and steady dark eyes. He wears a plain woven tunic of undyed wool in ochre-brown beneath a long cloak of dusty grey-blue wool. He carries a traveller's staff of dark wood and a leather bag at his hip.

payload.name: Mizpah (Gilead assembly place)
payload.note: The Gileadite gathering place in Judges where Jephthah speaks before Yahweh and the war against Ammon is organized; distinguished by the Judges setting and Gilead context.

stages.label: Mizpah (Gilead assembly place)

quotes.quote: The children of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpah.
Jephthah spoke all his words before Yahweh in Mizpah.

stages.text: Mizpah: a high ridge of pale limestone and red-brown earth in the hill country of Gilead, terraced for gathering. Flat open ground at its crest is ringed by low dry-stone walls and a few squat mud-brick and stone shrines with plain lintels. Scattered terebinth and oak stand at the edges, with olive groves and grey scrub on the slopes below.

payload.name: Bethel (conquered town of Joseph's house)
payload.note: Town in Judges taken by the house of Joseph, also where Israel seeks God's counsel in the war against Benjamin; note the Luz alias here matches the Genesis town, but this entry is the Judges conquest and counsel setting.

stages.label: Bethel (conquered town of Joseph's house)

quotes.quote: The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and Yahweh was with them.
The man went into the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called its name Luz
between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim
went up to Bethel, and asked counsel of God.

stages.text: Bethel: a walled hill town in the highlands of Ephraim on a stony ridge above a highway running north to Shechem and south toward Gibeah. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs stand close together behind a fortified gate and rough stone wall. Terraced slopes bear olive and fig trees, with scrub oak on the rocky ridges. A high place with standing stones marks the sacred ground where the people seek counsel.

payload.name: Gibeah of Benjamin (Judges)
payload.note: The Benjamite city where the Levite's concubine is abused and killed and that is the scene of the war against Benjamin in Judges; distinguish from Saul's Gibeah in 1 Samuel by the Judges events of the concubine and the war.

stages.label: Gibeah of Benjamin

quotes.quote: the sun went down on them near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin
He went in, and sat down in the street of the city
The children of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.

stages.text: Gibeah of Benjamin: a fortified hill town of the Benjamite highlands, set on a rocky ridge with terraced slopes. Low houses of mud brick and stone stand close together along a narrow street, flat roofs, and a city wall with a gate. Olive trees, vines and scrub grow on the slopes, with open fields and highways running out of the town.

payload.title: David's victories and officials

aliases: the anointed of the God of Jacob
payload.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
payload.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

payload.name: Joab
payload.note: Son of Zeruiah and David's army commander, who kills Abner, Absalom and Amasa and leads the Ammonite campaign; distinguish from other Joabs by his role as David's commander in the army.

stages.label: Joab, captain of David's army

quotes.quote: Joab was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a sword fastened on his waist in its sheath
He took three darts in his hand and thrust them through Absalom’s heart
Ten young men who bore Joab’s armor surrounded and struck Absalom

stages.text: Joab: a man in his middle years, around forty to fifty, of strong, weathered build with broad shoulders and a soldier's stance. Skin olive-brown and sun-browned. Dark hair cropped short at the neck, with a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey at the chin. Hard, watchful face with a broken nose. Signature outfit: a bronze-scaled or leather-plated military coat over a dark undertunic, with a deep red-brown war sash at the waist. Carries a sword in a plain sheath and three darts in hand.

payload.name: Benaiah son of Jehoiada (Kings)
payload.note: Captain of David's army and guard who carries out Solomon's executions in 1 Kings; the same Benaiah son of Jehoiada named here as one of the mighty men and later bodyguard commander.

stages.label: Benaiah son of Jehoiada

quotes.quote: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did these things and had a name among the three mighty men.

stages.text: Benaiah son of Jehoiada: a seasoned man of about forty to fifty, broad-shouldered and sturdy from years of combat, with dark skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard shot with grey, a weathered, steady face with a firm mouth and deep-set eyes. His signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic under a dark brown wool cloak with a deep red border, with bronze scale armour and a leather belt; he wears a bronze helmet. He carries a bronze-headed spear and a curved sword.

payload.title: Curses and expulsion from the garden

payload.name: Adam
payload.note: The first man formed from dust in Eden, husband of Eve and father of Cain, Abel and Seth; the Genesis narrative figure, joined by the 1 Corinthians and 1 Timothy references to the same first man.

stages.label: Adam

quotes.quote: there he put the man whom he had formed
to cultivate and keep it
Yahweh God made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.
All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred thirty years, then he died.

stages.text: Adam: a full-grown man in early middle age, sturdy and weathered from labour in the ground; broad shoulders, lean strong arms, dark brown skin darkened by sun; short dark curly hair and a close-cut beard; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen wrap over one shoulder, later a simple garment of tawny animal skin; sandals of leather. No signature props, though he is often shown with a hoe or digging tool.

payload.name: Eve
payload.note: The first woman in Genesis, made from Adam's rib and deceived by the serpent; the other two entries (2 Corinthians 11:3 and 1 Timothy 2:14) refer back to this same Eve.

stages.label: Eve

quotes.quote: she would be the mother of all the living

stages.text: Eve: a woman in early adulthood, slender and strong, with a grounded, unhurried bearing. Warm olive-brown skin, dark eyes, long black hair bound back with a linen band. Her face is open and calm, with a serious, dignified expression. Signature outfit: a simple undyed linen wrap over one shoulder, falling to the knee, in ochre and sand tones. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: the serpent of Eden
payload.note: The subtle serpent of the garden who deceives Eve and is cursed in Genesis; the Corinthians reference points back to this same serpent.

stages.label: The serpent of Eden

quotes.quote: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made.
you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the field. You shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.

stages.text: The serpent of Eden: an adult serpent of the field, long and sinuous, its body sleek and scaled in dull olive and dark ochre banded with pale bone-yellow, with a broad flattened head and cold, watchful eyes. Before the curse it is upright-bodied, slender and graceful, showing it was more subtle than the animals of the field; afterward it lies low, dusty, and close to the ground.

payload.name: Garden of Eden
payload.note: The garden planted by Yahweh God in Genesis, with the tree of life and forbidden tree; distinct from the garden in Song of Solomon and the garden across the Kidron.

stages.label: Garden of Eden

quotes.quote: Yahweh God planted a garden eastward, in Eden
including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.
he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way

stages.text: Garden of Eden: a well-watered garden planted eastward in Eden, lush with pleasant trees bearing good fruit, the tree of life and the tree of knowledge standing in its middle. A single river issues from Eden, parting into four streams that water the ground. Soft green grass and fertile dark soil, with reeds along the banks. At the eastern edge, a boundary of cherubim and a flaming sword.

payload.title: Who is greatest

aliases: the apostle and high priest of our confession
the great shepherd of the sheep
the author and perfecter of faith
the mediator of a new covenant
the Lion of the tribe of Judah
the rider called Faithful and True
KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS
payload.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
payload.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

payload.name: The Twelve Disciples (collective)
payload.note: The twelve apostles/disciples as one collective body acting together across the Gospels and Acts; distinct from the individual disciples named within them.

stages.label: The Twelve Disciples (collective)

quotes.quote: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

stages.text: The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

payload.name: Capernaum
payload.note: The lakeside town in Galilee where Jesus lives, teaches and heals, with a synagogue and Simon Peter's house; all four Gospels' entries describe this one place.

stages.label: Capernaum

quotes.quote: Leaving Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali
They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.
They entered into the boat, and were going over the sea to Capernaum.

stages.text: Capernaum: a fishing town of plain basalt and limestone houses with flat roofs, packed close along a curving shore of the Sea of Galilee. A white limestone synagogue with a tall carved doorway stands near the water, its pillars facing the lake. Nearby, a modest family house of stone with a courtyard and reed-thatched roof marks Simon's home. Fishing boats are drawn up on the stones, nets hung on poles. Olive trees, palms and fig trees grow on the slopes behind the town, with dry hills rising beyond.

payload.title: Indictment of Jerusalem's sins

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
payload.name: Jerusalem
payload.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

payload.title: Eliphaz on the fate of the wicked

payload.name: Eliphaz the Temanite
payload.note: Oldest of Job's three friends, from Teman; first to speak in the dialogues and recounts a night vision.

stages.label: Eliphaz the Temanite

quotes.quote: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite

stages.text: Eliphaz the Temanite: a man of about sixty, lean and upright; olive-brown skin weathered by desert sun; short grey-streaked beard trimmed close; deep-set, thoughtful eyes and a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a dark russet wool cloak. Carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: Job
payload.note: Blameless, wealthy man of Uz who loses his family and health and debates with his friends and with Yahweh.

stages.label: Job

quotes.quote: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

stages.text: Job: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifty to sixty, of sturdy but weathered build; dark brown skin; short, graying hair with a close-trimmed beard shaved at the head in grief; dignified, lined face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak over it. Carries a shepherd's staff of olive wood. Sores on skin in later sections.

payload.name: The ash heap
payload.note: Place outside the city where Job sits, scraping his sores with a potsherd (2:8).

stages.label: The ash heap

quotes.quote: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust

stages.text: The ash heap: a broad low mound of grey and white ash, dust and broken clay outside the city walls, sloping gently to bare dry ground. Scattered potsherds, cracked jars and cinders lie in drifts; sparse scrub and thorn bushes grow at its edges. Distant city walls, gates and roofs of sun-baked brick rise on the horizon.

payload.title: Fear God: the whole duty of man

payload.name: The Preacher (Qoheleth)
payload.note: First-person narrator-speaker of Ecclesiastes, presented as a son of David and king in Jerusalem who tests pleasure, labor and wisdom; the book never names him as Solomon.

stages.label: The Preacher (Qoheleth)

quotes.quote: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.

stages.text: The Preacher: a man of middle years, roughly fifty, lean and upright with a settled, reflective bearing. Olive-brown skin, close-cut dark hair and a short trimmed beard streaked faintly with grey at the chin. Deep-set, thoughtful eyes and a lined brow. Wears a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep blue royal court robe with a narrow gold border. He carries a plain wooden scroll case at his belt.

payload.name: Under the sun
payload.note: The general setting of earthly human activity described throughout; not a single place.

stages.label: Under the sun

quotes.quote: under the sun
all that is done under the sky
If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth

stages.text: Under the sun: a wide, sun-bleached Levantine earth of dry hill country and terraced fields, with stone walls, olive and terebinth trees, winding river beds, and distant walled cities of pale limestone beneath an open sky.

payload.title: Wisdom's public call and her worth

payload.name: Wisdom
payload.note: The personified figure Lady Wisdom who calls in the streets, builds a seven-pillared house, and speaks in Proverbs 1, 3, 4, 8 and 9; not a human woman.

stages.label: Wisdom as radiant presence

quotes.quote: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the entry doors, she cries aloud:
Wisdom has built her house. She has carved out her seven pillars.

stages.text: Wisdom: no human face or body; she is shown only as radiance, a pale luminous brightness gathered like light at a city gate, unbounded and warm. Her presence is light and voice, never a figure to be drawn as a woman.

aliases: the high places of the city
payload.name: The streets and city gates
payload.note: Public squares and gates of a city where Wisdom cries out and judgment is given; distinct from Jerusalem as a named city.

stages.label: The streets and city gates

quotes.quote: Wisdom calls aloud in the street. She utters her voice in the public squares.
Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the entry doors, she cries aloud:
She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,

stages.text: The streets and city gates: a walled town of packed earth and mudbrick and dressed stone on a low hill, with a broad double city gate of cedar-banded timber set in thick stone towers. Beyond the gate the public square is paved with flat limestone slabs, worn pale by feet. Mud-plastered houses of two storeys line narrow lanes; flat roofs, lintels, and stone benches stand by the gate. Olive trees and terraced vines grow on the slopes, with a tall high place of cut stone above the square.

payload.title: Jehu kills Joram at Naboth's field

aliases: son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi
payload.name: Jehu son of Jehoshaphat
payload.note: Captain anointed by a young prophet who kills Joram and Jezebel; not the prophet Jehu son of Hanani.

stages.label: Jehu, captain turned king

quotes.quote: Then he said, "I have a message for you, captain."
So Jehu rode in a chariot and went to Jezreel

stages.text: Jehu: a man of about forty-five, lean and hard-muscled from years of war and chariot driving; weathered tan skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with early grey; a broad, resolute face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic under a dark red military cloak, with bronze scale armour on the shoulders. Carries a composite bow and a short sword.

payload.name: Jehoram son of Ahab
payload.note: Named king of Israel, son of Ahab, who campaigns against Moab with Judah and Edom and is later killed by Jehu at Jezreel; the named individual that the unnamed king of Israel in the Naaman and Samaria sections is identified with.

stages.label: Jehoram son of Ahab, king of Israel

quotes.quote: Jehoram the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria
Jehu drew his bow with his full strength, and struck Joram between his arms

stages.text: Jehoram son of Ahab: a man in his prime, roughly forty to fifty years of age; lean, strong and weathered from campaigning; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a neatly trimmed beard; a grave, watchful face. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep blue royal court robe with a woven band of ochre at the hem and a bronze-scaled military belt. Props he alone carries: a plain gold signet ring and a royal bow.

payload.name: Bidkar
payload.note: Captain who helps cast Joram's body on Naboth's plot.

stages.label: Bidkar, captain of Jehu

quotes.quote: Then Jehu said to Bidkar his captain, “Pick him up, and throw him in the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite

stages.text: Bidkar: a seasoned soldier of about forty-five, sturdy and weathered, with bronze-brown skin from sun and road. Short dark hair under a plain headcloth, close-cut beard streaked with grey. Strong brow, steady eyes, a scarred cheek. Signature outfit: a dark-blue military tunic with a sleeveless leather jerkin over it, belted at the waist, and a faded ochre cloak. Carries a bronze-bladed short sword at his hip.

aliases: king of Judah son of Jehoram
payload.name: Ahaziah of Judah
payload.note: Judean king son of Jehoram, killed by Jehu; distinct from Ahaziah of Samaria.

stages.label: Ahaziah of Judah

quotes.quote: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem.
Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem.

stages.text: Ahaziah of Judah: a young king near twenty-two, lean and sinewy from chariot riding; warm olive skin; dark hair worn to the shoulder and a short, close-trimmed beard; a grave, watchful face with a high brow. Signature outfit: a long blue-violet royal tunic under a deep red woollen cloak with a gold-embroidered hem. Carries a plain bronze-bound bow case and a short sword with an ivory hilt.

aliases: the plot of Naboth the Jezreelite
payload.name: Naboth's field
payload.note: Vineyard plot where Joram is killed and thrown.

stages.label: Naboth's field
stages.text: Naboth's field: a terraced vineyard on a gentle slope below the walls of Jezreel, rows of low vines on stone-cleared earth, a dry-stone boundary wall, an old fig tree and a stone winepress cut into the rock at one edge, with the Jezreel valley and distant hills beyond.

payload.title: Recital of the patriarchs and the Exodus

payload.name: Egypt
payload.note: The land of Egypt where patriarchs sojourn, Israel is enslaved and plagues fall; recurs in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Psalms, Ezekiel, Hosea, Micah and Hebrews as the same land.

stages.label: Egypt

quotes.quote: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land.
Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen
But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them
for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.

stages.text: Egypt: a long green valley of the Nile flanked by pale desert; broad river channels, canals and reed marsh; fertile black earth fields of barley and flax; date palms and sycamores; mud-brick and limestone cities with tall temple pylons, obelisks and fortified walls; the Delta with its towns of Goshen and Zoan.

payload.title: Laban pursues and searches for the teraphim

payload.name: Laban
payload.note: Brother of Rebekah in Haran; hosts Jacob, gives him Leah and Rachel, and makes a covenant with him at Gilead.

stages.label: Laban of Haran

quotes.quote: Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.
When Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house.

stages.text: Laban: a man in his middle years, past youth but vigorous, with a sturdy build from herding and travel. Skin weathered olive-brown. Dark hair cropped close at the neck, a short full beard greying at the chin. Calm, watchful eyes and a broad, lined face. Signature outfit: a long undergarment of undyed wool beneath a rust-red wool mantle, leather sandals, a leather belt at the waist. Carries a herdsman's staff of dark wood.

payload.name: Jacob
payload.note: Younger twin son of Isaac and Rebekah, renamed Israel after wrestling with God and father of the twelve sons; the central patriarch of Genesis, also referenced by name in Hosea, Obadiah, Malachi and the New Testament letters.

stages.label: Jacob

quotes.quote: The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
Isn’t he rightly named Jacob?
his hand had hold on Esau’s heel
leaning on the top of his staff.

stages.text: Jacob: a slender, wiry man of middle to later years in his prime and sixties-to-seventies in old age; lean, sinewy build from long herding; smooth, unhairy skin browned by sun; dark, close-cropped hair and short beard kept trim; alert, thoughtful eyes and a clean, quiet face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and wool wrap cloak in earth brown, with leather sandals. Carries a shepherd's staff.

payload.name: Rachel
payload.note: Younger daughter of Laban, beloved wife of Jacob, mother of Joseph and Benjamin; dies in childbirth.

stages.label: Rachel

quotes.quote: Rachel was beautiful in form and attractive.
Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she kept them.

stages.text: Rachel: a young woman of about eighteen to twenty-five, slender and graceful, of good height; warm olive-brown skin, dark almond eyes, full dark brown hair worn long and bound with a linen band; fine, attractive features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a deep indigo wool wrap over the shoulders, simple leather sandals. Signature prop: a wooden shepherd's staff.

payload.name: Gilead
payload.note: Mountain in Gilead where Laban and Jacob make their covenant; the Genesis Gilead, not any other mountain here.

stages.label: Gilead, mountain country

quotes.quote: he rose up, passed over the River, and set his face toward the mountain of Gilead.
Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Laban with his relatives encamped in the mountain of Gilead.
a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing spices and balm and myrrh

stages.text: Gilead: high rocky mountain country east of the River, terraced hillsides of grey limestone and red earth, scattered oak and terebinth, wild grass and thorn scrub, dry watercourses between ridges, distant hills fading to blue, a few mud-brick and stone shelters at the edges, goat tracks, balm and spice shrubs on the slopes.

payload.title: Prayer in Gethsemane

payload.name: Simon Peter
payload.note: The fisherman apostle, first-called disciple and leader of the twelve, who appears in the Gospels, Acts, Galatians and both letters of Peter; all entries here are the same individual, distinguished only by role and portrayal.

stages.label: Simon Peter

quotes.quote: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas

stages.text: Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.

payload.name: James son of Zebedee
payload.note: Fisherman disciple called with his brother John in Matthew; distinct from James son of Alphaeus.

stages.label: James son of Zebedee

quotes.quote: James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets.
James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);

stages.text: James son of Zebedee: a man in his late twenties to thirties; lean, strong build from hauling nets; weathered olive-brown skin; short dark curly hair and a close-trimmed beard; steady, earnest eyes and a sun-lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown with a dark wool cloak in faded blue-grey. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

payload.name: John the apostle, son of Zebedee
payload.note: Fisherman apostle, brother of James son of Zebedee, appearing in Matthew, Luke and Acts; distinct from John the Baptist and John Mark.

stages.label: John the apostle

quotes.quote: in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets
who were partners with Simon

stages.text: John the apostle: young man of about twenty-five to thirty; lean, strong fisherman's build; sun-browned skin; dark brown hair falling to the shoulders, short beard; clear, earnest eyes and a steady, youthful face. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in earth tones with a dark brown wool cloak, sleeves rolled. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

aliases: the place where they went to pray
payload.name: Gethsemane
payload.note: Garden where Jesus prays and is arrested, named in Matthew and Mark; in Luke the same place is called the garden on the mount, on the Mount of Olives, so it is one place with three names.

stages.label: Gethsemane

quotes.quote: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane
They came to a place which was named Gethsemane.

stages.text: Gethsemane: a walled garden on the slope of the Mount of Olives, above the city of Jerusalem. Ancient gnarled olive trees with silver-grey leaves and thick trunks; dry limestone and red earth underfoot; low stone wall with a wooden gate; a press-stone and rough stone terrace; pale rock outcrops at the edge.

payload.title: Covenant with death and the foundation stone

payload.name: Isaiah son of Amoz
payload.note: Prophet who advises Hezekiah; the same prophet across Isaiah, 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

stages.label: Isaiah son of Amoz

quotes.quote: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your sandals from off your feet.

stages.text: Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. Dark hair graying at the temples, worn to the shoulders, and a short, full grey beard. Deep-set, steady eyes and a long, lined face marked by years of hard counsel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.
